_note: Hand-translated English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 5 (first encounter with Pharaoh fails; bricks-without-straw decree; foremen beaten; Moses complains to God). Key Saadia moves: v.1 יחגון לי = 'celebrate a festival to me' (Saadia for יחגו לי — pilgrimage festival); v.3 כילא יפאגינא בובא או בסיף = 'lest plague or sword come suddenly upon us'; v.4 תגד'באן = 'distract / draw away' (Saadia for תפריעו); v.5 אהל אלבלד = 'the people of the land'; v.6,10 גלאוזאת / גלאוזה = 'taskmasters' (now established in gloss); v.6,10,13 ערפא / ערפאהם = 'overseers / foremen' (Saadia's word for the Hebrew שטרים — the Israelite-appointed sub-foremen); v.7 תבנא = 'straw'; v.7 לילבנון אללבן = 'to mold bricks'; v.7 יקמשון = 'gather/glean' (the stubble); v.8 צ'ראיב = 'quotas/levies'; v.8 מרפהון = 'idle / at ease' (Saadia for נרפים); v.13 כמלו עמלכם = 'fulfill your work'; v.14 צ'ראיבכם = 'your quotas'; v.16 מצ'רובין ממא יכ'טי עליהם קומך = 'beaten because your people sin against them' (Saadia treats Israel's pleas as legitimate grievance); v.21 ינצ'ר אללה עליכם ויחכם = 'May God look upon you and judge'; v.21 אפסדתמא חאלנא = 'you have ruined our condition'; v.22 אבלית הולאי אלקום = 'you have brought trial upon this people'; v.23 אסא אליהם = 'has dealt evil with them'.

translations.1: And after that, Moses and Aaron entered, and said to Pharaoh: 'Thus says God, the God of Israel: Let my people go, that they may celebrate a festival to me in the wilderness.'
translations.2: Pharaoh said: 'Who is God, that I should accept from him and let the sons of Israel go? I do not know God; and I will not let the sons of Israel go either.'
translations.3: They said: 'The God of the Hebrews has caused His decree to come upon us. Let us go now a distance of three days into the wilderness, and offer sacrifice to the Lord our God — lest plague or sword come suddenly upon us.'
translations.4: The king of Egypt said to them: 'Why, Moses and Aaron, do you distract the people from their works? Go to your burdens!'
translations.5: And Pharaoh said: 'Now the people of the land are many — and you would have them rest from their burdens!'
translations.6: And Pharaoh commanded on that day the taskmasters of the people, and their overseers, saying:
translations.7: 'You shall no longer give the people straw to mold bricks, as yesterday and before; let them go and gather straw for themselves.
translations.8: And the quota of bricks which they were making yesterday and before — set [the same] upon them; you shall not reduce from it. For they are idle; therefore they cry out, saying: Let us go offer sacrifice to our Lord.
translations.9: Let the labor be heavy upon the people, and let them be occupied with it; and let them not be occupied with vain matters.'
translations.10: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their overseers, and said to them: 'Thus says Pharaoh: I am giving you no straw.
translations.11: You — go, take straw for yourselves from where you can find it. And know that there shall be nothing reduced from your work.'
translations.12: And the people scattered throughout all the land of Egypt, to gather stubble for straw.
translations.13: And the taskmasters pressed [them], saying: 'Finish your work — the matter of each day, on its day — just as it was when straw was given.'
translations.14: And the overseers of the sons of Israel — whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them — they beat, and said to them: 'What is the matter with you that you have not finished your quotas to mold bricks, as yesterday and before, both yesterday and today?'
translations.15: And the overseers of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying: 'Why do you act thus toward your servants?
translations.16: No straw is supplied to your servants; yet they are saying to us: Make bricks! And behold, your servants are beaten — because your people sin against them.'
translations.17: He said: 'You are idle, idle — therefore you say: Let us go and offer sacrifice to our Lord.
translations.18: And now, go, labor — and no straw shall be given to you; and your quotas you shall complete.'
translations.19: And the overseers of the sons of Israel saw [themselves] in evil, saying: 'You shall not reduce from your bricks — the matter of each day, on its day.'
translations.20: And they encountered Moses and Aaron, standing to meet them at their coming out from before Pharaoh.
translations.21: And they said to them: 'May God look upon you and judge — for you have ruined our condition before Pharaoh and before his officers; so that, were a sword in their hands, they would kill us.'
translations.22: And Moses returned to God, and said: 'O my Lord, why have You brought trial upon this people? And to what end have You sent me?
translations.23: For from the time I went in to Pharaoh to speak with him in Your name, he has dealt evil with them — and You have not rescued them from this.'
